subject: Chemistry
description: First law, second law, exothermic / endothermic, entropy, Gibbs free energy, Hess's law

questions.stem: An EXOTHERMIC reaction is one in which:

options.option_text: Heat is absorbed from the surroundings into the system
Heat is released from the system into the surroundings
Mass is created from energy stored in the chemical bonds
Reactants are converted but no temperature change happens

questions.explanation: EXOTHERMIC — releases heat (ΔH < 0). Surroundings warm up. Examples: combustion (CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + heat), neutralisation (acid + base), respiration (glucose + O₂), most precipitation. ENDOTHERMIC — absorbs heat (ΔH > 0). Surroundings cool down. Examples: photosynthesis, melting, evaporation, dissolving NH₄NO₃ in water (cold pack). Distractor 1 = endothermic. Distractor 3 — mass is conserved in chemical reactions; only energy form changes. Distractor 4 — there is always some thermal change.

questions.stem: The FIRST LAW of thermodynamics states that:

options.option_text: Heat always flows from cold bodies to hot bodies spontaneously
Energy can be neither created nor destroyed, only transformed
Entropy of an isolated system is always increasing over time
Absolute zero of temperature can be reached in finite steps

questions.explanation: FIRST LAW — energy conservation, applied to thermodynamic systems. Mathematically: ΔU = q − w (or q + w, sign convention varies); change in internal energy = heat added minus work done by the system. Forbids perpetual-motion machines of the FIRST kind. Distractor 1 — opposite of true; heat flows from hot to cold (Second Law / Clausius). Distractor 3 = SECOND law (entropy increase). Distractor 4 = THIRD law violation (absolute zero is unreachable in finite steps).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: ENTROPY (S) is best described as a measure of:

options.option_text: The total internal energy stored in the system
The disorder or number of microscopic arrangements
The rate at which the chemical reaction proceeds
The total mass of substances in the system

questions.explanation: ENTROPY — measure of disorder / number of microstates. Boltzmann formula: S = k ln W (W = number of accessible microstates; k = Boltzmann constant). Higher disorder → higher entropy. Examples — ice (low S) → water (medium S) → vapour (high S). Mixing two gases increases entropy. SECOND LAW: total entropy of universe always increases in any spontaneous process. Distractor 1 = internal energy U. Distractor 3 = rate constant. Distractor 4 = mass.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Gibbs FREE ENERGY change (ΔG) determines spontaneity. A reaction is spontaneous at constant T, P when:

options.option_text: ΔG is positive and grows larger over time
ΔG is negative (free energy decreases)
ΔG is exactly zero (system at equilibrium)
ΔG is undefined under these conditions

questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS. Spontaneity criterion at constant T, P: ΔG < 0 (free energy decreases). ΔG = 0 → equilibrium (no net change). ΔG > 0 → non-spontaneous (reverse is spontaneous). EXOTHERMIC + entropy-increasing reactions are always spontaneous. ENDOTHERMIC + entropy-decreasing are always non-spontaneous. The other two combinations depend on temperature: high T favours entropy-driven processes, low T favours enthalpy-driven processes.

questions.stem: HESS'S LAW states that the total enthalpy change of a chemical reaction is:

options.option_text: Always equal to twice the activation energy of the reaction
Independent of the path taken to convert reactants to products
Proportional to the temperature at which it is carried out
Negligible compared to entropy of the system in question

questions.explanation: HESS'S LAW — enthalpy is a STATE FUNCTION; total ΔH depends only on initial and final states, NOT on the route. Practical use: if a reaction can't be measured directly (e.g., burning C to CO is hard to control vs CO₂), we sum up other measurable steps to get the desired enthalpy. Born-Haber cycle uses Hess's law to compute lattice enthalpies. Distractor 1 — confuses ΔH with Ea. Distractor 3 — wrong proportionality. Distractor 4 — false generalisation.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The SECOND LAW of thermodynamics implies that:

options.option_text: Heat always flows spontaneously from cold to hot bodies
Total entropy of an isolated system never decreases over time
Energy can be created from nothing in a closed system
Absolute zero is reachable using any cooling method available

questions.explanation: SECOND LAW — entropy of an isolated system never decreases; it stays the same in reversible processes and increases in irreversible (real) processes. Equivalent statements: (a) Heat flows spontaneously from hot to cold, never the reverse without external work — Clausius. (b) No engine working between two reservoirs can be 100% efficient at converting heat to work — Kelvin-Planck. (c) Forbids perpetual-motion machines of the SECOND kind. Distractor 1 — opposite of correct direction. Distractor 3 violates first law. Distractor 4 violates third law.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Burning a fuel to release stored chemical energy as heat is an example of:

options.option_text: An endothermic reaction with positive ΔH
An exothermic reaction with negative ΔH
A reaction with zero enthalpy change overall
A reaction that violates the first law of thermodynamics

questions.explanation: Combustion = exothermic; energy of bonds in reactants > energy of bonds in products → difference released as heat. Standard enthalpies of combustion: methane −890 kJ/mol; ethanol −1367 kJ/mol; petrol/octane −5470 kJ/mol; hydrogen −286 kJ/mol (cleanest, no CO₂). Bond enthalpies determine ΔH. Distractor 1 — endothermic = absorbs heat (e.g., photosynthesis, melting). Distractor 3 — combustion has large negative ΔH. Distractor 4 — combustion conserves energy (heat output = bond energy difference); doesn't violate any law.
